sentence: The notices that were printed by the council contain the new collection dates.
setupText: Choose the shorter description that preserves who printed the notices.
taskText: The notices that were printed by the council contain the new collection dates.
text: Choose the shorter description that preserves who printed the notices. The notices that were printed by the council contain the new collection dates.
options: The notices printed about the council contain the new collection dates.
The notices printed by the council contain the new collection dates.
The notices printed for the council contain the new collection dates.
The notices sent to the council contain the new collection dates.
answer: The notices printed by the council contain the new collection dates.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2921:Shortening a passive relative while retaining its agent
explanation: Removing that were retains the passive printed by the council and the original printing agent.

rationales.The notices printed about the council co: About the council makes the council the topic of the notices, not their printer.
rationales.The notices printed for the council cont: For the council identifies a beneficiary or intended user, not necessarily the printer.
rationales.The notices printed by the council conta: Removing that were retains the passive printed by the council and the original printing agent.
rationales.The notices sent to the council contain: Sent to names the recipient rather than the organization that printed the notices.

sentence: Guests who are leaving before breakfast should return their keys tonight.
setupText: Choose the shortened instruction that preserves the selected group.
taskText: Guests who are leaving before breakfast should return their keys tonight.
text: Choose the shortened instruction that preserves the selected group. Guests who are leaving before breakfast should return their keys tonight.
options: Guests leaving after breakfast should return their keys tonight.
Guests leaving before breakfast should return their keys tonight.
Guests staying for breakfast should return their keys before leaving.
Guests returning their keys tonight should leave before breakfast.
answer: Guests leaving before breakfast should return their keys tonight.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2922:Active reduction preserves the domain of an instruction
explanation: Leaving before breakfast preserves the group described by who are leaving before breakfast.

rationales.Guests leaving before breakfast should r: Leaving before breakfast preserves the group described by who are leaving before breakfast.
rationales.Guests leaving after breakfast should re: After changes which departures the instruction concerns.
rationales.Guests staying for breakfast should retu: Staying for breakfast selects a different group and removes tonight as the return deadline.
rationales.Guests returning their keys tonight shou: This tells key-returners when to depart instead of telling early leavers when to return their keys.

sentence: Complete the message: The furniture ___ will go into the new office.
setupText: Choose the description that says the delivery is happening now, not finished or merely planned.
taskText: Complete the message: The furniture ___ will go into the new office.
text: Choose the description that says the delivery is happening now, not finished or merely planned. Complete the message: The furniture ___ will go into the new office.
options: being delivered now
delivered last week
to be delivered next month
ordered but not yet delivered
answer: being delivered now
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2923:Being plus past participle describes an ongoing passive event
explanation: Being delivered keeps passive meaning and marks the delivery as currently in progress.

rationales.delivered last week: Delivered last week presents a completed past delivery, not one in progress.
rationales.being delivered now: Being delivered keeps passive meaning and marks the delivery as currently in progress.
rationales.to be delivered next month: To be delivered next month describes a future plan, not an ongoing delivery.
rationales.ordered but not yet delivered: Not yet delivered describes delivery as still outstanding rather than happening now.

sentence: The bicycles repaired yesterday are ready for collection.
setupText: Choose the meaning of 'repaired' in this sentence.
taskText: The bicycles repaired yesterday are ready for collection.
text: Choose the meaning of 'repaired' in this sentence. The bicycles repaired yesterday are ready for collection.
options: The repairs to those bicycles were completed yesterday.
The bicycles are waiting for repairs to begin.
The bicycles will be repaired when collected.
The bicycles are being repaired during collection.
answer: The repairs to those bicycles were completed yesterday.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2924:A completed passive descriptor identifies a ready group
explanation: The past-participle description 'repaired yesterday' identifies the bicycles by completed repair work.

rationales.The bicycles are waiting for repairs to: 'Repaired yesterday' identifies bicycles whose repairs have already taken place, not those awaiting a start.
rationales.The bicycles will be repaired when colle: 'Yesterday' places the repair in the past; collection is the next available step.
rationales.The bicycles are being repaired during c: The sentence says the bicycles are ready for collection, not still being repaired during it.
rationales.The repairs to those bicycles were compl: The past-participle description 'repaired yesterday' identifies the bicycles by completed repair work.

sentence: Priya checked the attachments. Then she sent the email to Dan.
setupText: Choose the version that keeps Priya as the person who checked and sent the email.
taskText: Priya checked the attachments. Then she sent the email to Dan.
text: Choose the version that keeps Priya as the person who checked and sent the email. Priya checked the attachments. Then she sent the email to Dan.
options: After checking the attachments, Priya sent the email to Dan.
After checking the attachments, Dan sent the email to Priya.
After sending the email to Dan, Priya checked the attachments.
After Dan checked the attachments, Priya sent the email.
answer: After checking the attachments, Priya sent the email to Dan.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2925:A shared subject in an introductory after-ing clause
explanation: Priya is the main subject and the understood subject of checking, preserving her two actions in order.

rationales.After checking the attachments, Dan sent: The main subject Dan becomes the understood checker and sender, reversing both roles.
rationales.After checking the attachments, Priya se: Priya is the main subject and the understood subject of checking, preserving her two actions in order.
rationales.After sending the email to Dan, Priya ch: This puts sending before checking, reversing the sequence.
rationales.After Dan checked the attachments, Priya: This gives the checking to Dan, although Priya performed it in the original.

sentence: On arriving at the venue, report to the reception desk.
setupText: Choose the meaning of 'on arriving' in the instruction.
taskText: On arriving at the venue, report to the reception desk.
text: Choose the meaning of 'on arriving' in the instruction. On arriving at the venue, report to the reception desk.
options: Before travelling to the venue
While choosing a venue
When you arrive at the venue
After leaving the reception desk
answer: When you arrive at the venue
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2926:On plus ing marks an event that triggers the next action
explanation: 'On arriving' is a concise way to say 'when you arrive', making arrival the cue to report.

rationales.Before travelling to the venue: 'On arriving' locates the action at arrival, not before the journey.
rationales.While choosing a venue: 'Arriving' describes reaching the chosen venue, not selecting one.
rationales.When you arrive at the venue: 'On arriving' is a concise way to say 'when you arrive', making arrival the cue to report.
rationales.After leaving the reception desk: The report follows arrival and takes you to reception; it is not scheduled after leaving reception.

sentence: Before setting off, the driver checked the route with the passenger.
setupText: Choose the version that keeps the driver, rather than the passenger, responsible for checking the route.
taskText: Before setting off, the driver checked the route with the passenger.
text: Choose the version that keeps the driver, rather than the passenger, responsible for checking the route. Before setting off, the driver checked the route with the passenger.
options: Before they set off, the passenger checked the route for the driver.
After they set off, the driver asked the passenger to check the route.
While the driver set off, the passenger finished checking the route.
Before they set off, the driver checked the route with the passenger.
answer: Before they set off, the driver checked the route with the passenger.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2927:Expanding a time participle phrase without shifting responsibility
explanation: The driver remains the checker and checking stays before departure; with the passenger preserves the companion's involvement.

rationales.Before they set off, the driver checked: The driver remains the checker and checking stays before departure; with the passenger preserves the companion's involvement.
rationales.Before they set off, the passenger check: This changes the checker to the passenger rather than the driver.
rationales.After they set off, the driver asked the: This shifts the check until after departure and assigns it to the passenger.
rationales.While the driver set off, the passenger: This moves checking into the departure period and makes the passenger the checker.

sentence: Not knowing the address, Elena called her host for directions.
setupText: Choose the meaning of the opening phrase.
taskText: Not knowing the address, Elena called her host for directions.
text: Choose the meaning of the opening phrase. Not knowing the address, Elena called her host for directions.
options: Elena's host did not know the address.
Elena called to tell her host the address.
Elena refused to give her host the address.
Elena did not know where she needed to go.
answer: Elena did not know where she needed to go.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2928:A negative participle phrase states a subject's lack of knowledge
explanation: Not knowing the address describes Elena's missing information and explains her request for directions.

The opening phrase has Elena as its understood subject, not her host.
rationales.Elena called to tell her host the addres: Elena is seeking directions because she lacks the address; she is not supplying it.
rationales.Elena refused to give her host the addre: Not knowing describes lack of information, not unwillingness to share known information.
rationales.Elena did not know where she needed to g: Not knowing the address describes Elena's missing information and explains her request for directions.

sentence: The residents were woken by the alarm. They went outside.
setupText: Choose the description that keeps the alarm as the cause and the residents as the people affected.
taskText: The residents were woken by the alarm. They went outside.
text: Choose the description that keeps the alarm as the cause and the residents as the people affected. The residents were woken by the alarm. They went outside.
options: Alerted by the residents, the guard went outside.
Woken by the alarm, the residents went outside.
After going outside, the residents tested the alarm.
Woken by the residents, the guard switched off the alarm.
answer: Woken by the alarm, the residents went outside.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2929:An introductory passive participle shares the main subject
explanation: The residents are the understood recipients of woken, and by the alarm preserves the cause.

rationales.Alerted by the residents, the guard went: This gives the alert to a guard and makes the residents its source, changing the affected people.
rationales.Woken by the alarm, the residents went o: The residents are the understood recipients of woken, and by the alarm preserves the cause.
rationales.After going outside, the residents teste: This substitutes an alarm test after going outside for being woken before going outside.
rationales.Woken by the residents, the guard switch: This introduces a guard as the person woken and gives the residents the waking role.

sentence: Use a short description beginning with 'Applicants'.
setupText: Choose the instruction addressed to people who received an invitation, not people sending one.
taskText: Use a short description beginning with 'Applicants'.
text: Choose the instruction addressed to people who received an invitation, not people sending one. Use a short description beginning with 'Applicants'.
options: Applicants preparing invitations should confirm a date.
Applicants inviting the panel should confirm a date.
Applicants requesting invitations should confirm a date.
Applicants invited to an interview should confirm a date.
answer: Applicants invited to an interview should confirm a date.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2930:Passive versus active role in a concise audience description
explanation: 'Invited' is passive and identifies applicants who have received an interview invitation.

rationales.Applicants preparing invitations should: 'Preparing invitations' describes producing them, not receiving one.
rationales.Applicants inviting the panel should con: 'Inviting' makes applicants the senders of an invitation to the panel.
rationales.Applicants invited to an interview shoul: 'Invited' is passive and identifies applicants who have received an interview invitation.
rationales.Applicants requesting invitations should: Requesting an invitation does not establish that one has been received.

sentence: The last delegate to arrive missed the introductions but joined the discussion.
setupText: Choose the person described as the last to arrive.
taskText: The last delegate to arrive missed the introductions but joined the discussion.
text: Choose the person described as the last to arrive. The last delegate to arrive missed the introductions but joined the discussion.
options: The delegate who left after the discussion
The delegate who introduced the discussion
The delegate who arrived after the other delegates
The delegate who arrived before the introductions
answer: The delegate who arrived after the other delegates
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2931:An infinitive after last identifies a position in an event sequence
explanation: To arrive after last identifies the delegate at the end of the arrival sequence.

rationales.The delegate who left after the discussi: Last to arrive orders arrivals, not departures after the meeting.
rationales.The delegate who arrived after the other: To arrive after last identifies the delegate at the end of the arrival sequence.
rationales.The delegate who introduced the discussi: The delegate missed the introductions and is not described as giving them.
rationales.The delegate who arrived before the intr: Missing the introductions is consistent with arriving late, not with the stated earlier arrival.

sentence: There are still three customers for me to serve before I go home.
setupText: Choose the meaning of the infinitive description.
taskText: There are still three customers for me to serve before I go home.
text: Choose the meaning of the infinitive description. There are still three customers for me to serve before I go home.
options: The speaker still needs to serve three customers.
The speaker has finished serving three customers.
A colleague will serve three customers after the speaker leaves.
Three customers have finished using the self-service counter.
answer: The speaker still needs to serve three customers.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2932:A for-me infinitive identifies the actor of a remaining task
explanation: For me to serve identifies both the remaining action and the speaker who must perform it.

rationales.The speaker has finished serving three c: Still...to serve describes remaining work, not service already completed.
rationales.A colleague will serve three customers a: For me identifies the speaker as the server, and before I go home places the work before departure.
rationales.Three customers have finished using the: The infinitive assigns service to the speaker, not to customers who have already served themselves.
rationales.The speaker still needs to serve three c: For me to serve identifies both the remaining action and the speaker who must perform it.

sentence: There is nobody waiting outside, so we can close the desk.
setupText: Choose the full meaning of the shortened description.
taskText: There is nobody waiting outside, so we can close the desk.
text: Choose the full meaning of the shortened description. There is nobody waiting outside, so we can close the desk.
options: Everyone waiting outside has left the desk open.
Someone outside is waiting for the desk to close.
No one inside is allowed to wait outside.
No one is waiting outside.
answer: No one is waiting outside.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2933:An ing description after nobody under an existential statement
explanation: Nobody waiting outside means that no person is currently waiting there.

Nobody waiting outside means that no person is currently waiting there.
rationales.Everyone waiting outside has left the de: The sentence denies an outside waiting group; it does not report that such a group left anything open.
rationales.No one inside is allowed to wait outside: The statement concerns whether people are waiting, not permission for people inside to wait elsewhere.

sentence: Keep the receipt and contact the shop again if necessary.
setupText: Choose the fuller version of 'if necessary' that preserves the instruction.
taskText: Keep the receipt and contact the shop again if necessary.
text: Choose the fuller version of 'if necessary' that preserves the instruction. Keep the receipt and contact the shop again if necessary.
options: if the shop asks to see the receipt
if you need to contact the shop again
if the shop has already contacted you
if you are required to buy another item
answer: if you need to contact the shop again
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2934:Recovering the event omitted after if necessary
explanation: 'If necessary' means 'if further contact is needed' in the context of this instruction.

rationales.if the shop asks to see the receipt: A request to see the receipt is one possible situation, not the general need expressed by 'if necessary'.
rationales.if the shop has already contacted you: The phrase does not limit further contact to cases where the shop contacted you first.
rationales.if you need to contact the shop again: 'If necessary' means 'if further contact is needed' in the context of this instruction.
rationales.if you are required to buy another item: The possible necessity concerns contacting the shop, not buying something else.

sentence: Although tired, Nabil stayed to help clear the room.
setupText: Choose the meaning of the opening phrase.
taskText: Although tired, Nabil stayed to help clear the room.
text: Choose the meaning of the opening phrase. Although tired, Nabil stayed to help clear the room.
options: Nabil stayed so that he could rest before helping.
Nabil stayed until he became tired.
Nabil was tired, but he stayed to help.
Someone tired asked Nabil to stay.
answer: Nabil was tired, but he stayed to help.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2935:An adjective clause reduced after although
explanation: Although tired expands to although Nabil was tired, contrasting his state with his decision to stay.

rationales.Nabil stayed so that he could rest befor: The phrase gives a contrasting state, not a plan to rest before helping.
Although tired expands to although Nabil was tired, contrasting his state with his decision to stay.
Tiredness is already present, not a later endpoint introduced by until.
Nabil is the understood tired person, and no request from someone else is stated.

sentence: Put the forms to be signed in the manager's tray.
setupText: Choose the meaning of 'to be signed' in this instruction.
taskText: Put the forms to be signed in the manager's tray.
text: Choose the meaning of 'to be signed' in this instruction. Put the forms to be signed in the manager's tray.
options: Put the forms the manager has already signed there.
Put the forms awaiting a signature there.
Put the forms containing the manager's signature there.
Put the forms the manager refused to sign there.
answer: Put the forms awaiting a signature there.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2936:A passive infinitive describes a pending action on a noun
explanation: 'To be signed' is a passive infinitive describing a task still required for those forms.

rationales.Put the forms the manager has already si: 'To be signed' presents signing as still to happen, not completed.
rationales.Put the forms containing the manager's s: An existing signature is not what the future passive description identifies.
rationales.Put the forms the manager refused to sig: Awaiting signature does not mean the manager has refused to sign.
rationales.Put the forms awaiting a signature there: 'To be signed' is a passive infinitive describing a task still required for those forms.

sentence: After being asked to lower the volume, the tenant switched off the music.
setupText: Choose the meaning that preserves who received the request.
taskText: After being asked to lower the volume, the tenant switched off the music.
text: Choose the meaning that preserves who received the request. After being asked to lower the volume, the tenant switched off the music.
options: The tenant asked a neighbour to switch off the music.
The tenant made the music louder before asking for help.
Someone asked the tenant to make the music quieter.
The tenant asked for permission to play music.
answer: Someone asked the tenant to make the music quieter.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2937:After being plus a participle retains passive agency
explanation: Being asked is passive: the tenant receives the request before switching off the music.

rationales.Someone asked the tenant to make the mus: Being asked is passive: the tenant receives the request before switching off the music.
rationales.The tenant asked a neighbour to switch o: The tenant is the person being asked, not the person giving the request to a neighbour.
rationales.The tenant made the music louder before: Lower the volume asks for quieter music; no earlier increase or request for help is reported.
rationales.The tenant asked for permission to play: The request concerns lowering existing sound, not permission to begin playing music.

sentence: The employee who is covering reception will answer your call.
setupText: Choose the shorter description that preserves the employee's current assignment.
taskText: The employee who is covering reception will answer your call.
text: Choose the shorter description that preserves the employee's current assignment. The employee who is covering reception will answer your call.
options: The employee covering reception will answer your call.
The employee covered by reception will answer your call.
The employee to cover reception tomorrow will answer your call.
The employee who covered reception last week will answer your call.
answer: The employee covering reception will answer your call.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2938:Active reduction retains the time supplied by a current progressive context
explanation: Covering reception removes who is while retaining the employee's current active assignment.

rationales.The employee covered by reception will a: Covered by is passive and does not describe the employee providing reception cover.
rationales.The employee to cover reception tomorrow: Tomorrow changes a current assignment into a future one.
rationales.The employee covering reception will ans: Covering reception removes who is while retaining the employee's current active assignment.
rationales.The employee who covered reception last: Last week replaces the current assignment with an earlier one and does not shorten the description.

sentence: Keep both the description of the jacket and the main statement that it belongs to me.
setupText: Choose the grammatical sentence in standard written English.
taskText: Keep both the description of the jacket and the main statement that it belongs to me.
text: Choose the grammatical sentence in standard written English. Keep both the description of the jacket and the main statement that it belongs to me.
options: The jacket hanging beside the stairs belonging to me.
The jacket hangs beside the stairs belongs to me.
The jacket hanging beside the stairs belongs to me.
The jacket which hanging beside the stairs belongs to me.
answer: The jacket hanging beside the stairs belongs to me.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2939:A participle description does not replace the finite main predicate
explanation: Hanging beside the stairs describes the jacket; belongs supplies the main statement.

rationales.The jacket hanging beside the stairs bel: Hanging and belonging are both non-finite forms here, leaving the sentence without a finite main verb.
Hanging beside the stairs describes the jacket; belongs supplies the main statement.
rationales.The jacket hangs beside the stairs belon: Hangs and belongs are two finite verbs without a clause link between them.
rationales.The jacket which hanging beside the stai: A full which clause would need is hanging; which cannot stand directly before hanging alone here.

sentence: Preserve that missing action in a short phrase with 'without'.
setupText: Choose the sentence that means the speaker did not stop to buy coffee.
taskText: Preserve that missing action in a short phrase with 'without'.
text: Choose the sentence that means the speaker did not stop to buy coffee. Preserve that missing action in a short phrase with 'without'.
options: After stopping for coffee, I drove to work.
Instead of driving, I stopped for coffee.
Before stopping for coffee, I drove to work.
Without stopping for coffee, I drove to work.
answer: Without stopping for coffee, I drove to work.
focusKey: coverage-reduced-clauses-b1-2940:Without plus ing expresses a non-occurring accompanying action
explanation: 'Without stopping' excludes the coffee stop from the drive to work.

rationales.After stopping for coffee, I drove to wo: 'After stopping' says a coffee stop happened before the drive.
rationales.Instead of driving, I stopped for coffee: 'Instead of driving' replaces the drive with the stop, changing both actions.
rationales.Before stopping for coffee, I drove to w: 'Before stopping' anticipates a coffee stop afterward rather than describing the drive without one.
rationales.Without stopping for coffee, I drove to: 'Without stopping' excludes the coffee stop from the drive to work.
